name: Declaration of Acquisition of Nationality

requirements.blocker_text: 5 years of legal, uninterrupted residence in Belgium (limited exceptions for those born in Belgium).

Must show social integration (upper-secondary-or-higher education credential, 400+ hours of recognised professional training, an integration course, or 5 years' continuous employment) OR economic participation (468+ days as a paid worker/civil servant within 5 years, or 6+ quarters of self-employed social security contributions).
Proof of knowledge of one of Belgium's three national languages (French, Dutch, German) -- generally satisfied automatically through demonstrating the integration standard above.
10 years of legal, uninterrupted residence for applicants unable to satisfy the social/economic integration standard of the 5-year route.

requirement_groups.name: Naturalisation on grounds of exceptional merit

requirements.blocker_text: A structurally distinct, rare process: proof of exceptional merit in scientific, sporting, or sociocultural fields, with the application submitted directly to the Chamber of Representatives (Parliament) rather than processed administratively via a municipal declaration. No fixed residence-duration requirement was confirmed for this route.

evidence_required.document: Proof of residence period matching the applicable route

sources.title: FPS Justice (Belgium.be) -- Declaration of Acquisition: 5-year residence + integration/economic-participation standard, or 10 years without it, EUR 150 fee, 4-month prosecutor review window

FPS Justice (Belgium.be) -- Citizenship: overview confirming naturalisation on exceptional-merit grounds is submitted to the Chamber of Representatives, distinct from the administrative declaration-of-acquisition route

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Belgium). 'Declaration of acquisition' is Belgium's standard administrative naturalisation-equivalent mechanism (processed by the municipality/royal prosecutor); 'naturalisation' in the strict Belgian legal sense is a SEPARATE, rare, parliamentary act reserved for exceptional merit, bundled here as a third requirement group rather than a separate file since both ultimately grant the same citizenship outcome via the be_naturalisation.json id. Also exists but not modeled as separate groups (to avoid excessive fragmentation): a 'declaration of attribution' for minors under 18 whose parents meet specific conditions, and modified/shorter residence periods for those with family ties to Belgian citizens or those unable to work due to disability, per justice.belgium.be's declaration-of-acquisition page -- disclosed here, not itemised.
